}","reasoning_content":"We need answer JSON statuses for R1-R5 based on Verified Claims C1-C2. Need determine support.

Original question asks identify scientific name of disorder shared by two cases. Task skeleton requirements:
R1: There were two cases in different years reported in 2010s.
R2: cases covered a particular disorder shared between two individuals.
R3: first case reported in a country that was the largest country of its dominant religion in world at time of establishment. In this case individual presented half-year history of pain in different parts body, pain worsened, causing difficulty walking and moving shoulders.
R4: another case individual presented complaints pain and swelling in upper part body, where procedure involving collection of tissue samples to test for disease had been performed two months earlier. When younger, developed stiffness, followed by swelling four years later.
R5: After evaluating these reports, what is scientific name of disorder both cases reported to have?

Verified Claims only C1 and C2 about Stiff person syndrome symptoms. They support maybe R2? R2: cases covered a particular disorder shared between two individuals. Claims describe Stiff person syndrome, but don't mention cases or two individuals or shared. They mention disorder name "Stiff person syndrome" but no case connection. Does that support R2? R2 requires cases covered a particular disorder shared. Claims don't establish cases, nor shared. They just describe disorder. Topical relevance/entity name maybe not enough. However, the question is asking disorder; if claims identify Stiff person syndrome symptoms, maybe partially support R2? Need material: "particular disorder shared between two individuals." The claims establish a disorder exists and its symptoms. But do not establish that the cases covered it or shared between individuals. Could count as partially supported? Need carefully.

R3: first case country + symptoms. C1/C2 mention symptoms: aching discomfort, stiffness, pain lower back/hips/legs, shoulders, arms, neck, progressive leg stiffness leads slow stiff walking. The R3 symptom part: half-year history of pain in different parts, gradually worsened, difficulty walking and moving shoulders. Claims support that Stiff person syndrome may cause pain, stiffness, shoulder involvement, walking difficulty. Not half-year history, not first case country. Partial support of symptom descriptions. But requirement includes country condition entirely unsupported. So partially_supported? At least one substantive material part (symptom profile) supported by C1/C2. The symptom in R3: pain in different parts, worsened, difficulty walking/moving shoulders. C2 says pain in lower back/hips/legs, may affect shoulders, arms, neck, progressive leg stiffness can lead to slow stiff manner of walking. C1 says symptoms develop over months to years, may slowly worsen. This matches partly: pain multiple body parts, worsening, walking difficulty, shoulder affected. It doesn't mention half-year history exactly, and no country. So partial.

R4: another case symptoms: pain and swelling in upper part body, biopsy two months earlier, when younger developed stiffness followed by swelling four years later. Claims mention stiffness/pain but not swelling, upper body? C2 mentions shoulders arms neck affected, pain/stiffness. No swelling, no biopsy, no temporal history. Does it establish at least one substantive part? It supports that disorder may cause pain and stiffness, maybe upper body/shoulders. R4 requires pain and swelling in upper part, procedure, childhood stiffness followed by swelling. Claims support "stiffness" and "pain" but no swelling. Is that a substantive part? Possibly partially_supported because pain and stiffness are material symptoms. However, R4's core is about another case presentation with swelling and biopsy. C1/C2 establish some symptoms of Stiff person syndrome, but not the specific presentation. The question requires identifying disorder from this report. If claims about Stiff person syndrome symptoms match some of the case, that's partial. But if R4 is a requirement to establish the case details, C1/C2 don't establish the case. They only state general disorder symptoms. Need decide.

R5: asks scientific name. Claims mention "Stiff person syndrome" but that's common name? Is it scientific name? Stiff person syndrome is a disorder, scientific name maybe "stiff-person syndrome" or "Moersch-Woltman syndrome"? Actually C1/C2 say "Stiff person syndrome" (common/scientific? The scientific name is Stiff person syndrome? The question asks scientific name; "Stiff person syndrome" is a medical term, not exactly scientific? But claims identify disorder name. Does that support R5? R5: After evaluating these reports, what is scientific name of disorder that both cases were reported to have? The claims don't say both cases had it, nor that it's the answer after evaluating. They mention Stiff person syndrome. Could be partial: they provide name of a disorder matching some symptoms, but not establish it is the disorder both cases reported. So partial maybe.

R1: two cases in different years reported in 2010s. No claims about cases, years, 2010s. Unsupported.

R2: cases covered a particular disorder shared between two individuals. Claims mention Stiff person syndrome but no cases/shared. Is any substantive part? The "particular disorder" part is established by claims: Stiff person syndrome. But "cases covered" and "shared between two individuals" unsupported. So partially_supported? The requirement essentially: there is a particular disorder shared by two individuals in the cases. Claims establish a disorder exists (Stiff person syndrome) but not that cases covered it or shared. That's one substantive part: the disorder identity. But is the disorder identity part of requirement? Yes, "particular disorder" is part. However, without cases/shared, partial. But maybe the claims don't establish "shared between two individuals"; they don't mention cases. But they establish the disorder name. So partial.

R3: partial as above.

R4: partial? Let's examine if claims establish any material part of R4. R4 has:
- another case
- individual presented complaints of pain and swelling in upper part of body
- where a procedure involving collection of tissue samples to test for disease had been performed two months earlier
- when younger, developed stiffness
- followed by swelling four years later.

C1/C2: stiffness, pain, shoulders/arms/neck, progressive. They support pain and stiffness, perhaps upper body. They do not support swelling, biopsy, timeline. So at least one substantive material part: pain and stiffness in upper body? C2: may affect shoulders, arms, neck; pain. Yes, pain in upper part maybe. Stiffness. So partial.

R5: The requirement asks scientific name. Claims provide "Stiff person syndrome" as name. But is that the answer? The claim says "Stiff person syndrome symptoms..." It establishes the name of a disorder. But R5 requires "scientific name of the disorder that both cases were reported to have". Claims don't establish both cases or that they were reported to have it. They just mention the disorder name. Partial? It supports the name of a disorder with matching symptoms. But not the connection to both cases. So partially_supported. Alternatively, if we interpret R5 as just asking for name, and claims mention Stiff person syndrome, that might fully support? No, because must be disorder both cases reported; claims don't establish cases. So partial.

Need ensure no fully_supported? Maybe none fully. Could R2 be fully? No. R5 partial.

But we need be precise: "For partially_supported, the cited Claims must establish a substantive material part of the requirement." For R1 none. R2? Does mentioning Stiff person syndrome establish "a particular disorder"? It establishes a disorder named Stiff person syndrome. That's a material part? The requirement says "The cases covered a particular disorder shared between two individuals." The material parts: (a) cases covered a disorder; (b) disorder shared between two individuals; (c) particular disorder. Claims establish (c) but not (a)(b). Is (c) substantive? The identity of the disorder is central to question. Yes. So partial.

R3: Claims establish some symptom details: pain different parts, worsening, walking difficulty, shoulder. They don't establish half-year history or country. So partial.

R4: Claims establish pain and stiffness, maybe upper body, but not swelling, biopsy, childhood timeline. Partial.

R5: Claims establish name "Stiff person syndrome" but not that both cases had it. Partial.

Unsupported: R1 only.

Need output JSON with requirement_id exactly once. Supported_by arrays with C1/C2 where applicable. For unsupported empty.

Need consider if we can cite C1 and C2 for each partial. Yes.

Let's craft final JSON only. Ensure valid JSON. Use statuses exactly. 

Let's produce:
{
  "requirements": [
    {"requirement_id": "R1", "status": "unsupported", "supported_by": []},
    {"requirement_id": "R2", "status": "partially_supported", "supported_by": ["C1","C2"]},
    {"requirement_id": "R3", "status": "partially_supported", "supported_by": ["C1","C2"]},
    {"requirement_id": "R4", "status": "partially_supported", "supported_by": ["C1","C2"]},
    {"requirement_id": "R5", "status": "partially_supported", "supported_by": ["C1","C2"]}
  ]
}

But check R5: C1/C2 mention "Stiff person syndrome". Is that enough to support "scientific name"? The term "Stiff person syndrome" is a name. But scientific name? There might be a more scientific name. However, the claim explicitly says "Stiff person syndrome symptoms". It establishes that term. So partial.

Could R2 be unsupported? The requirement is about cases covered a particular disorder shared between two individuals. Claims don't mention cases or individuals. They only describe the disorder. Is merely mentioning a disorder a substantive part of "cases covered a particular disorder shared"? The requirement is about the cases and sharing. The particular disorder is an entity. But without cases, the claim is background context? Rule 11: Mere topical relevance, entity-name overlap, candidate mention, prior search direction, or background context does not count as support. Here C1/C2 are about the disorder that likely is answer, but they don't mention cases. Is that entity-name overlap? They mention "Stiff person syndrome", which could be candidate answer. But the requirement R2 is "The cases covered a particular disorder shared between two individuals." If claims don't mention cases, they don't establish that cases covered it. The only part they establish is "a particular disorder" exists. But is that a material part of the requirement? The requirement's core is that the two cases shared a disorder. The identity of the disorder is material. However, the claim doesn't say it's the disorder in the cases. It's just a general description. Could be considered unsupported because no connection to cases. But the definition says partially_supported: Verified Claims establish at least one substantive material part of the requirement, but one or more material parts remain unsupported. If R2 material parts are: (1) two cases, (2) they covered a disorder, (3) the disorder is shared, (4) particular disorder identity. C1/C2 establish (4) as a disorder with symptoms. But do they establish "particular disorder" as the one in cases? No. They establish existence of a disorder. Is that enough? It might be too weak; it's not a material part of "cases covered a particular disorder shared between two individuals" because it doesn't tie to cases. But the requirement asks to identify the disorder. The identity is part. However, to identify the disorder, you need it to be the shared disorder. Without cases, it's just a candidate. Rule 11 says candidate mention does not count as support. "Stiff person syndrome" is a candidate mention. So maybe R2 should be unsupported. Similarly R5 might be unsupported? But R5 asks for scientific name. The claims give a name, but not establish it's the answer. Candidate mention? Hmm.

Let's think of how these verification tasks usually work. The Task Skeleton requirements are pieces of the original question. Verified Claims are facts that can support them. If a claim states "Stiff person syndrome symptoms..." and the question asks what disorder both cases have, does that claim support the answer? It provides the name of the disorder if the symptoms match. But the requirement R5 is "After evaluating these reports, what is the scientific name of the disorder that both cases were reported to have?" The claims don't mention the reports or both cases. They only mention a disorder name. That is likely partial because it provides the name of the disorder, but not the connection. But is it substantive? Yes, the name is the answer. However, without connection, it's not established as the answer. Partial seems appropriate.

For R2, the requirement is "The cases covered a particular disorder shared between two individuals." The claims establish a disorder name and symptoms, but not that cases covered it. Could be partial because it establishes the disorder identity. But if we are strict, the claim doesn't establish any case details. The requirement is specifically about the cases covering a shared disorder. The claims are about the disorder itself, not the cases. That might be considered background context for the disorder, not support for the requirement that the cases covered it. However, the requirement also requires the identity of the disorder. The claims provide that identity. So I lean partial.

For R3, the requirement includes both country and symptoms. Claims support symptoms partially. So partial.

For R4, claims support some symptoms (pain, stiffness) but not swelling, biopsy, timeline. Partial.

For R5, claims support the name. Partial.

What about R1? No support.

Need decide if R2 could be fully? No, because no cases.

Could R3 be unsupported? The country part is completely unsupported, and the symptom part is only partially matched. But it's a substantive part: symptoms of pain, worsening, walking difficulty, shoulder. C1/C2 match. So partial.

Could R4 be unsupported? The symptoms in R4: pain and swelling in upper part, biopsy, childhood stiffness followed by swelling four years later. Claims mention pain and stiffness, but not swelling. Does "pain and stiffness" constitute a substantive part of R4? R4 says "presented complaints of pain and swelling... When they were younger, they had developed stiffness..." So pain and stiffness are both mentioned. Claims support that the disorder can cause pain and stiffness, especially in upper body. So partial.

Thus final JSON as above.

Need ensure supported_by uses exactly claim IDs. For R1 empty. For others include C1, C2. Should we include both for each? Yes, collectively they support.
